memos.argument: If the cards carry mounted actual fuses (a fuse assortment card/kit for motor vehicles), the fuses are the goods and heading 8536 names fuses for voltage up to 1,000 V; 12 V automotive fuses fit 8536.10.00 (glass cartridge 20 vs other 40). The card is mere packaging under GRI 1/5.
exclusions_against: Fact missing: whether fuses are physically present; purely printed cards have no fuses
No relevant CROSS ruling on fuse cards found in my searches

memos.argument: As described, 'printed fuse cards' are printed cards (charts/identification of fuses), printed matter of heading 4911 not elsewhere specified; ch49 note 2 treats 'printed' broadly. Printed on paper by lithography would be 4911.99.60.00 but 4911.99.80.00 is the default. Rulings F81395 and F83047 show 4911 lines for printed articles/posters.
exclusions_against: Ch49 note 1 does not exclude fuses, but if actual fuses are mounted, the printed card is packaging and the fuses give essential character (8536)
Cited rulings are weakly analogous (posters, tinplate articles), not fuse cards

memos.argument: Heading 8538 covers parts suitable solely or principally for apparatus of 8535, 8536, 8537; a fuse card could be argued a part/accessory of fuse boxes (identification card for a fuse panel).
exclusions_against: Fuses themselves are in 8536, not parts of it
A printed chart is not a part that functions in the apparatus; weak fit
No ruling support found; navigate gave 8538.90 without a verified 10-digit code
